test_input: Hold UP for 120 frames, then alternate LEFT and RIGHT while holding UP to navigate the track. Cross the lap line. Press R. Press ESC.
notes:
Controls and exact console lines printed when they take effect:
- Up arrow (KEYDOWN): prints 'ACCELERATE' and applies forward acceleration while held.
- Down arrow (KEYDOWN): prints 'BRAKE' and applies braking/reverse while held.
- Left arrow (KEYDOWN): prints 'TURN LEFT' and rotates heading CCW while held.
- Right arrow (KEYDOWN): prints 'TURN RIGHT' and rotates heading CW while held.
- R (KEYDOWN): prints 'RESTART' and resets car position, velocity, heading, lap count to 0.
- Escape (KEYDOWN) or window close: prints 'QUIT' and exits.
- When a lap is completed by crossing the checkpoint then the start line: prints 'LAP COMPLETE'.

High level notes:
- Files: game/drift_car.py contains all gameplay, rendering, input, physics; game/__init__.py is an empty package initializer.
- Track: a donut-shaped track is rendered using filled rectangles (outer/inner) and two vertical lines for checkpoint and start line; walls are simple rect outlines per Plan.
- Physics: custom simple momentum/drift model: the car keeps a velocity vector separate from its heading; steering rotates heading but velocity retains lateral component which is damped over time to simulate drift. Friction reduces forward speed when not accelerating.
- Collision: rect-based collision with outer and inner boundaries. On collision the forward momentum is removed and the car is pushed back to its previous position.
- Assets: provided car_sprite.png and desert_canyon_background.png (if present) are loaded from game/assets. Background is scaled to the window size and used; if assets are missing the game draws procedural colors.
- Limitations/approximations:
  - The desert canyon environment is approximated by the supplied background image scaled to the window and simple colored shapes for cliffs/cacti are not procedurally drawn beyond the background image.
  - Collisions use axis-aligned rectangles (pygame.Rect) so corner cases near curved walls are approximate.
  - No sounds are implemented per Plan.

Play expectations (how to exercise automated checks):
- Hold UP for ~10 frames (0.16s) and observe console 'ACCELERATE' and increasing speed.
- Hold DOWN and observe console 'BRAKE' and decreasing/negative forward speed.
- Press and hold LEFT for ~10 frames; observe 'TURN LEFT' and heading rotating CCW.
- Press and hold RIGHT for ~10 frames; observe 'TURN RIGHT' and heading rotating CW.
- While turning at high speed, observe the car sprite move on a tangent (movement vector differs from heading) to see drift.
- Drive across the left checkpoint then around to the start line to see 'LAP COMPLETE' and lap counter increment.
- Press R to reset; observe 'RESTART' and laps reset to 0.
- Press ESC to quit; observe 'QUIT'.

Exact engine/run details:
- Resolution: 800x600, FPS: 60.
- Entry point: python -m game.drift_car or python game/drift_car.py

Known issues:
- Visual fidelity of the canyon is approximated by the provided background image; no dynamic lighting or particles.
- Collision and lap detection are based on rectangle bounds and x-crossings; very tight maneuvers may occasionally not register precisely.

Files implementing requirements:
- game/drift_car.py implements all gameplay, rendering and state management.
